logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of complexes Ir1 and Ir2, which was presented as octanol-water partition coefficient (Log Po/w), was determined using a classical shake-flask method.5 Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and water-saturated octanol (WSO) were prepared by shaking analytical grade octanol and 50 mM NaCl aqueous solution (to suppress hydrolysis of the chloride complex) together using a laboratory shaker for 24 h to allow saturation of both phases. Stock solutions of complexes were prepared in the aqueous phase at a concentration of 100 μM, and then were added to an equal volume of saturated 1-octanol phase. The resultant biphasic solutions were mixed for 4 h at 500 rpm at 310 K, and then centrifuged (3000 rpm, 5 min) to separate the phases. The concentrations of the complexes in the organic and aqueous phases were determined by UV-vis absorbance at 260 nm. Log Po/w was defined as the logarithm of the ratio of the concentrations of the complex in the organic and aqueous phases (LogPo/w = Log {[Au(org)]/[Au(aq)]}; values reported are the means of three separate determinations).
